latest.title: Beyond the Web Request: Scaling Background Jobs and Asynchronous Workloads on AWS
latest.description: When you build a modern web application—whether in Laravel, Node.js, or Python—most user interactions follow a synchronous request-response cycle: a client makes an HTTP request, the application server queries a database, computes business logic, and returns an HTML or JSON payload within a few hundred milliseconds.

latest.title: 🎨 The Joy of Creation: Why Building in the Cloud Feels Like Magic!
latest.description: Ever felt that instant spark of joy when your code finally works and goes live? 🎨 Cloud building isn't just about servers and syntax—it's pure creative magic! From turning crazy ideas into real apps to embracing the fun of learning along the way, here’s a lighthearted reminder of why we all fell in love with building in the first place. Read, smile, and get inspired to build something fun today! ✨

latest.title: Sending marketing email from Laravel with Amazon SES: what I wish I had set up on day one
latest.description: Lessons from building a small email CRM on Laravel and SES: leaving the sandbox, DNS authentication, queue throttling, handling bounces and complaints through SNS, and keeping contacts in sync with Shopify webhooks.

latest.title: DemoBuddy 2.0 🎤 — Teaching an AI Agent When to Ask, Hint, or Help
latest.description: What makes an AI agent enjoyable is not just its answers, but knowing what to do next. DemoBuddy is a project-rehearsal coach designed to help students practise presentations through adaptive questions, gentle hints, and honest demo-recovery plans. This next version explores using Strands Decider 2B for tool selection and Amazon Bedrock for natural, helpful responses.

trending.title: How we ran the Kiro University Challenge as a community build-along: 141 builders at AWS User Group Madurai
trending.description: A community case study and playbook from AWS User Group Madurai. We - Vivek, Logesh and Poobalan turned Kiro's seven-lesson University Challenge into a build-along with four evening Circle sessions, a one-command setup that created a compliant repo and progress tracking, a leaderboard ranked by active days, and community rewards earned by rank. 141 members joined, 77 linked a repo, 38 demonstrated all seven lessons. Includes the numbers, what went wrong, and how to run it without a custom platform.

trending.title: AWS Community Day Adria - A conference that changes lives and careers
trending.description: AWS Community Day Adria is the biggest AWS-related event in the Adriatic / Balkans region and the biggest AWS Community Day in Europe. Organized by the community, for the community.

trending.title: Benchmarking Strands Decider, LLM Classifiers and Bedrock Routing for Model Routing
trending.description: I routed 216 graded requests across Amazon Nova and Claude models with Strands Decider, five LLM classifiers, Bedrock Intelligent Prompt Routing and Bedrock Advanced Prompt Optimization. The decider judged request difficulty perfectly (ROC AUC 1.00 against 0.88 for Claude Sonnet 4.6) but cost about 0.0012 USD and 11 to 13 s per decision on a CPU microVM. Here are the numbers and the rules I now follow for when a decision model should judge and when a small LLM should route.

trending.title: Three Lessons from Kiro Nights Nairobi - Build, Break and Deploy with Kiro
trending.description: What creating a culture of innovation through the AWS AI/ML User Group Kenya taught us after organizing Kiro Nights Nairobi to Build, Break and Deploy with Kiro. Three lessons from a 2-hour buildathon using Kiro and deployment on AWS.

trending.title: How to Implement AWS KMS: Encryption at Rest Explained (2026 Guide)
trending.description: Learn AWS KMS encryption at rest with S3, IAM and key policies, Terraform examples, encryption enforcement, pricing, CloudTrail, and troubleshooting.

trending.title: Strands Box on AWS Lambda MicroVMs: a kernel per agent, a policy per command, and a fleet to run them with microvm-ctl
trending.description: Strands Box checks every shell command, file and request an agent makes against a Dogwood policy. Lambda MicroVMs give the agent its own kernel. I built Box for aarch64 Linux, ran it inside Lambda MicroVMs, and drove fleets with microvm-ctl: 83 ms per box, 22.7 boxes/s per 1 GB VM, 64 of 64 correct across 8 VMs, a playground app, and the bugs I hit.

trending.title: De Blind Spots a Claridad Total: Por Qué las Trazas Distribuidas Son Imprescindibles en Microservicios
trending.description: En la era de los monolitos, entender qué sucedía cuando un usuario hacía clic en un botón era relativamente sencillo: bastaba con revisar los registros agregados del servidor web y seguir la pila de llamadas (stack trace) en un único proceso.

trending.title: AWS Spend Limits: A Safer Way for Beginners to Learn Cloud!
trending.description: Are you also afraid to launch an EC2 instance because of unexpected AWS bills? 😰 Not anymore! ☁️ AWS is introducing project-level spend limits to help students and new developers experiment with greater confidence. Read the blog and start your cloud journey without the same fear of surprise bills!
